name_reason: Fully compliant with the global naming convention data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. Domain = dialog/shop; descriptor 'no_equip' accurately names the reject prompt ('no one can equip this'); 'text_id_table' reflects the data type (table of FDTXT page text-ids). No Ghidra address residue; the '6' dimension and 0..5 index are real domain semantics (per-shop-tier), not address artifacts.
purpose: Per-shop-tier FDTXT dialog page text-id table for the 'no one can equip this' reject prompt shown when a gear item has zero equip-capable recipients in the chapter-intro shop BUY flow.
logic_summary: int16[6] const table indexed by data_fd2_chapter_intro_menu_cursor_state @ 0x5412B (0..5, shop-tier radio). Sole reader fd2_run_buy_item_menu (DATA @ 0x2F0E1 + READ @ 0x2F0E6) block-copies the 12 bytes via 3x MOVSD into a stack-local, then on the gear/no-eligible-candidate branch reads it back as a signed 16-bit word (MOVSX word ptr [base + cursor_state*2]) and passes the value as the FDTXT page id to fd2_display_dialog_scene. The *2 stride + MOVSX word access confirms int16 (signed) elements; index range 0..5 gives the 6-element dimension. One of five sibling per-tier dialog tables consecutive in .object2 (inventory_full/buy_for/no_money/no_equip/auto_equip).
element_semantics: element[shop_tier] = FDTXT.DAT page text-id for the 'no one can equip this' reject message for that shop tier; value passed directly as the page id to fd2_display_dialog_scene. Content {1, 505, 1, 437, 1, 437}: tiers 0/2/4 -> FDTXT[1] (default fallback), tier 1 -> FDTXT[505], tiers 3/5 -> FDTXT[437].
notes: src comment block (dlgtab.c lines 90-109) was already accurate, precise, terse: documents purpose, sole reader fd2_run_buy_item_menu @ 0x2F0E6, 3x MOVSD copy + MOVSX word access, *2 stride, 6-element dimension, read-only/no writers, and values matching memory exactly. Left unchanged (comment_verdict=keep). Const confirmed: only 2 xrefs (both reads, DATA @ 0x2F0E1 + READ @ 0x2F0E6) from fd2_run_buy_item_menu; zero writers.
